neighbours.label: judging a thing's intrinsic nature: 'in and of itself', 'per se', 'inherently', 'morally neutral' (not good or bad as such)
fire: Ambition is not a vice in and of itself, though it can lead people astray.
Critics do not object to wealth per se, only to the way it was acquired.
Nobody claims that competition is inherently harmful to young athletes.
A knife is morally neutral; everything depends on the hand that holds it.
Caffeine is not intrinsically dangerous, but large doses can cause problems.
The technology itself is neither good nor bad, whatever its critics believe.
There is nothing wrong with eating meat as such, the author argues.
Debt isn't necessarily a bad thing in itself if it pays for an education.
quiet: Ambition drove him out of his village, though it later led him astray.
Critics do not object to the film's length, only to the way it ends.
Nobody claims that competition has grown tougher for young athletes this year.
A knife lay on the counter; everything else had been cleared from the kitchen.
Caffeine is found in tea and coffee, and large doses can keep you awake.
The technology arrived late in the region, whatever its critics believe.
There is nothing left to eat in the fridge, the author complains.
Debt rose last year in most provinces as families paid for education.
